title: Write a restrained Strudel groove with a real turn
summary: Compose executable Strudel that establishes a pocket, develops it without crowding, and earns one turnaround.
originNote: A recognizable live-coding composition control focused on groove, restraint, form, and variation rather than code volume.

setup.instructions: Mount the musical brief and bounded syntax crib. Produce standalone Strudel source; do not fetch packages or samples.

turns.content: Read fixtures/brief.json and fixtures/strudel-crib.md. Write a runnable Strudel piece to main.strudel. It must establish the pocket, create a B section by changing the musical relationship rather than merely adding density, use one turnaround to make the return feel earned, and leave deliberate space. Mark the structural regions with comments // A, // B, and // TURNAROUND. Write listening-notes.md with no more than 160 words explaining the pocket, what B changes, and what to listen for in the return. Do not spend the note explaining basic syntax.

Revise the same piece so the turnaround uses fewer events than the densest bar but creates a stronger sense of arrival through placement, register, silence, or timbre. Preserve the established pocket and B section. Update both files.

checks.description: The source names all three structural regions and uses a sounding pattern.
Render in Strudel and listen for pocket continuity, a relational B section, deliberate space, and an earned return.
